task_instance: In a sample repo containing a real CLAUDE.md and real skill content under .claude/skills/formatting/, set it up for multiple agents: migrate CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md as the canonical instruction file (never creating CLAUDE.md), and create a relative symlink so the shared skills directory is not duplicated (.claude/skills holds the content, so .agents/skills links to ../.claude/skills).
evidence: Work dir real2_work/r024/sample-repo. Created sample repo: real CLAUDE.md (build/style instructions) and .claude/skills/formatting/SKILL.md. Applied skill decision table: 'CLAUDE.md real, AGENTS.md absent' -> ran 'mv CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md'. Applied the skill's shared-skills branch '.claude/skills has real content' with CANON_SKILLS=.claude/skills, CONSUMER_SKILLS=.agents/skills, CONSUMER_SKILLS_TARGET=../.claude/skills, and ran the skill's safe-linking shell block verbatim, producing '.agents/skills -> ../.claude/skills'. Verification: CLAUDE.md absent (no file, no dangling symlink); AGENTS.md readable with original content fully preserved; 'ls -la .agents' shows 'skills -> ../.claude/skills' (relative link); readlink -f resolves into sample-repo/.claude/skills; the consumer link exposes formatting/SKILL.md (cat through .agents/skills/formatting/SKILL.md succeeded). Idempotency: re-running the link logic detected the existing correct symlink, preserved its direction, and left the setup working. No git/network/credentials/MCP used; all work confined to the work directory.
